(WebFetch extract of Kyiv Independent, Aug 8 2026; cross-ref Mezha/Ukrainska Pravda.)

Zelensky makes first-ever official visit to Serbia, Aug 8 2026.

- Zelensky arrived in Belgrade for his first official visit to Serbia during his presidency; met President Aleksandar Vucic at the Palace of Serbia (meetings began Aug 7, two-day visit), with a planned meeting with PM Duro Macut.
- Agenda: expanding economic ties, relations with the EU / joint EU accession (opening negotiating clusters), security, energy cooperation, sanctions against Russia, and the "Carpathian Initiative" - a new regional format involving Ukraine, Serbia, Romania, Austria, Hungary, Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

Zelensky quotes:
- "We will discuss expanding economic ties between our countries, relations with the European Union, other areas that can benefit our nations, and security issues."
- "Ukraine is always ready to work constructively, for mutual benefit, and on the basis of mutual respect."

Significance:
- Symbolic given Serbia's historical alignment with Russia. Serbia has balanced between Moscow and the West since Russia's 2022 invasion, relying on Russia for energy while (per reports) indirectly supplying arms to Ukraine, which Vucic publicly denied in May 2025.
- Vucic did not sign a joint declaration at the June 2025 Ukraine-Southeast Europe summit condemning Russian aggression and reaffirming Ukraine's territorial integrity.
- Vucic posted a photo of himself hugging Zelensky during the visit.
